Let \(p=101\). We count how many times each exponent \(n\) appears.

For \(n\ge 1\), define

\[
C_n=\#\{(j,k):1\le j\le p-1,\ k\ge 1,\ \lfloor pk/j\rfloor=n\}.
\]

Since all terms are nonnegative,

\[
S=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\sum_{j=1}^{p-1}2^{-\lfloor pk/j\rfloor}
=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} C_n 2^{-n}.
\]

For fixed \(j,n\),

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{pk}{j}\right\rfloor=n
\iff
\frac{jn}{p}\le k<\frac{j(n+1)}{p}.
\]

Write \(jn=qp+t\), where \(0\le t\le p-1\). The interval becomes

\[
q+\frac{t}{p}\le k<q+\frac{t+j}{p}.
\]

Since \(j/p<1\), there is at most one integer \(k\).

- If \(t=0\), then \(p\mid jn\), and since \(p\) is prime and \(1\le j\le p-1\), we have \(p\mid n\). For \(n\ge1\), \(q\ge1\), so \(k=q\) works.
- If \(t>0\), the only possible integer is \(q+1\), which works iff

\[
q+1<q+\frac{t+j}{p}
\iff
t+j\ge p+1.
\]

Thus, if \(p\nmid n\), then \(j\) contributes to \(C_n\) exactly when

\[
j+(jn\bmod p)\ge p+1.
\]

This depends only on \(r\equiv n\pmod p\).

Now evaluate \(C_n\) by \(r\):

- If \(r=0\), then every \(j\) contributes, so \(C_n=p-1\).
- If \(r=p-1\), then \(jn\bmod p=p-j\), so \(j+(p-j)=p\), and no \(j\) contributes.
- If \(1\le r\le p-2\), pair \(j\) with \(p-j\). Let \(t_j\equiv rj\pmod p\), \(1\le t_j\le p-1\). Then \(t_{p-j}=p-t_j\), and

\[
(j+t_j)+((p-j)+t_{p-j})=2p.
\]

Also \(j+t_j\ne p\), since that would imply \(r\equiv -1\pmod p\). Hence exactly one element of each pair satisfies the inequality. There are \((p-1)/2\) pairs, so

\[
C_n=\frac{p-1}{2}.
\]

For \(p=101\), this gives

\[
C_{101m}=100,\qquad
C_{101m+r}=50\ (1\le r\le 99),\qquad
C_{101m+100}=0.
\]

Thus \(C_n\) is periodic with period \(101\), and

\[
S=\frac{\sum_{n=1}^{101}C_n2^{-n}}{1-2^{-101}}.
\]

Now

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{101}C_n2^{-n}
=
50\sum_{n=1}^{99}2^{-n}+100\cdot 2^{-101}.
\]

Since \(\sum_{n=1}^{99}2^{-n}=1-2^{-99}\),

\[
50(1-2^{-99})+100\cdot 2^{-101}
=50-\frac{25}{2^{99}}
=\frac{25(2^{100}-1)}{2^{99}}.
\]

Therefore

\[
S=
\frac{25(2^{100}-1)}{2^{99}}\cdot \frac{2^{101}}{2^{101}-1}
=
\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}}
\]
